hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 7
hunts.subtitle: A sliver of moon, a damp mild dawn, and bucks who have other things on their minds.

rules.title: Saturday checklist (clocks already changed Nov 1)
items: **Hunter orange** on, hat and vest (required Oct 17 to Jan 1 for firearm hunters).
**Real hunting is legal light, 6:05 am, to about 9:00 am.** Be unloaded and out by 9:00.

**Dove and Coastal-zone ducks reopen today.** Both are opportunity only. Any migratory bird needs your HIP number and a 3-shell plug. Ducks also need the federal duck stamp, the state waterfowl privilege and steel shot only.
**Crow is open on Saturdays.** HIP and plug apply.
rules.note: Confirm seasons, bag limits and shooting hours in the NCWRC Regulations Digest. Check that your phone and watch both show the new time.

conditions.source: Source: hourly forecast from a commercial weather service (the National Weather Service point forecast page was out of date). Sun times from a published sun table.
items: **Walk-in, 4:50 am:** about 55°F. Light northwest breeze, 3 to 4 mph. Partly cloudy. Humidity 97 to 98%, so wet leaves and dew.
**9 am:** about 56°F. North-northwest wind near 8 mph. Partly cloudy.
**Precipitation:** 11% or less all morning. Dry. Afternoon high near 64°F.
**Moon:** waning crescent, about 7% lit. Moonrise listed near 3:57 am, so a thin sliver sits low in the east. New moon is Monday.
conditions.meaning: **What it likely means (my assumption, not proven):** a mild, damp start turning breezy. Deer often move best right at first light, and a dark moon can push more feeding into daylight. The wind builds past 6 mph after 7, which covers small noises but also pushes deer to sheltered edges.
conditions.hours_note: No gust figures were listed. Coldest point is about 7 am. The wind climbs from 3 to 8 mph, so the thread will lean harder after 8.

wind.label: from the north-northwest, 3 mph at the walk-in rising to 8 mph by 9 am

in_season: **Deer, either sex** (gun season, day 22). Seeking phase: bucks are on their feet checking does.

in_season.text: **Dove** (second segment Nov 7 to Nov 28). Opportunity only.
in_season.tip: Needs HIP and a 3-shell plug. #7.5, birds crossing to the north only, never low, never toward the house or field.

in_season.text: **Coastal-zone ducks** reopen today (Nov 7 to 28). Skip unless you own steel shot.
in_season.tip: Needs HIP, federal duck stamp, state waterfowl privilege, steel shot and the plug. Never carry lead shot while duck hunting.

in_season: **Crow** (Saturday is an open day) and **snipe**: opportunity only with HIP and plug.
Closed: woodcock (opens Dec 10). Quail opens Nov 21. Turkey is a spring season.

in_season.tip: Bobcat is open. Bear opens next Saturday, Nov 14. You are not hunting either. Slugs stay zipped, for defense only.

plan.title: The plan: the Loop North Elbow, wind in your face near the swamp
plan.why: **Why here:** the loop trail's north end bends back toward the swamp. Sit about 40 yards south of the water, a few steps off the trail, facing N and NE. The wind comes from the NNW, so it blows into your face. Your scent drifts SSE, behind you, away from the swamp corridor. Deer that come up from the swamp thickets or along the water edge walk into the wind and toward you. **Approach:** come in from the south along the loop interior, so your scent never crosses the area ahead of you. **Timing:** legal light is 6:05. Be seated by 5:20, about 45 minutes before. Leave the yard at 4:50. **Caution:** a deer on your south side would smell you. Turn your head, never the gun. This is new ground for you, and it teaches you where the loop meets the swamp.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail with the red light low. Three steps, listen, three steps. Count your steps.
At the loop trail, turn onto it and follow it north through the center. Keep the swamp ahead of you.
About 40 yards before the water, stop. Step a few yards off the trail and pick a trunk wider than your shoulders. Nothing south of you matters; check what is behind every lane you will use.
Sit with your back to the trunk, facing N and NE. Load at the sit, muzzle north, safety on. Tie the thread to the barrel. If it points toward the swamp instead of SSE, slide 20 yards and sit again.
Legal light. Scan in sectors, near, middle, far. The first half hour of light is the best window.
No deer? Stay put. A dark moon and a rising wind can still bring a buck through. Move only your eyes.
Swap 00 for #4. Walk the swamp edge west, slow, into the wind. Squirrel and rabbit. Shoot N, NW, NE, E or W only.
Walk the route you would use to drag a deer from the sit to the yard. Count the steps.
Unloaded and out at the yard edge. Log what you saw with a "note:" message.

items: **In the gun:** 00 buckshot in the magazine. Modified choke. Safety on. Plug in.
**Right pocket:** #4 and #7.5 birdshot. Swap in at about 8:30.
**Also carry:** knife, hatchet, gloves, 12-inch thread, 10 feet of cord, a dry layer.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
Never shoot buckshot or slugs without the ground behind the target.
Keep buckshot and birdshot in different pockets. Check by feel.
Steel only for ducks. Do not carry lead shot while duck hunting.

animals.name: Deer
paragraphs: **Local:** common. They bed in the swamp thickets and travel the water edge and the pines.
**Today:** seeking phase, dark moon, mild, wind in your face. Best window (assumption): 6:05 to 7:30.
**Shot:** broadside or quartering away only. 30 yards maximum with 00. Aim just behind the front shoulder, mid-body. Shoot only N, NW, NE, E or W. Never south.

details.title: Technique: hear it before you see it
steps: A walking deer makes an uneven, four-beat step: crunch, pause, crunch-crunch, pause. A squirrel is fast and random.
When you hear the uneven rhythm, stop moving. Turn only your eyes toward it.
Look low and through the gaps between trunks, not at the sky line. You are looking for legs first.
Note the direction and wait. Do not raise the gun until you see a clear body, the ground behind it, and a lane that is N, NW, NE, E or W.
details.note: Wet leaves are quiet today. Your ears will tell you less than usual, so trust movement and flicks.

after: **Tip:** if you take a deer, tag it right away and look up the reporting steps in the Regulations Digest tonight, before you need them.
**Tip:** a mild morning means meat warms fast. Plan to open and cool it within the hour.

animals.name: Squirrel
paragraphs: **Local:** gray squirrels are seen often. Fox squirrel is possible.
**Today:** damp leaves keep them quiet early. Feeding picks up as the sky clears around 6. (Assumption.)
**Shot:** head and neck. #4 to 30 yards, #7.5 to 25 yards. Only with a trunk or the ground behind it.

details.title: Technique: watch the cutters under the pines
steps: Look for pine cone scales and fresh husks piled at a trunk base. That is a feeding table.
Stand 25 yards off, behind a trunk, and watch the crown above the pile.
Wait 10 to 15 minutes without moving. The squirrel returns to the same limb.
Shoot only when the head is in the open and a trunk or the ground is behind it.

after: **Tip:** scales that are still wet or sticky with sap are fresh. Dry gray ones are old.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: **Local:** likely at the feed bins and along thick edges of the loop.
**Today:** dew is heavy, so a rabbit's path shows as a dark line through wet grass.
**Shot:** #4 to 30 yards, N, NW, NE, E or W only.

details.title: Technique: follow the dew trail
steps: Look for a dark trail brushed through wet grass or leaves, ending at a thicket.
Follow it slowly into the wind.
Stop 15 yards short of the thicket and wait a full minute.
If it bolts south, let it go.

after: **Safety:** wear gloves when you handle it and check the liver for white spots.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Opportunity only. One heading to a den at dawn is possible near the swamp edge or the bins.
**Look for:** scat with seeds and berry skins on logs, and overturned leaf litter. Hair snagged on bin edges.
**Shot:** #4, head and neck, 20 yards, with a trunk or the ground behind. Never toward the house or field.

animals.name: Dove and crow (opportunity)
paragraphs: **Dove:** the season reopens today. They feed in open fields, so most traffic is off your land. A bird over the pines is a bonus.
**Crow:** open on Saturdays. Take one only with a clear northern sky. #7.5, plug in, HIP on you.
**Rule:** both need the 3-shell plug and HIP.

details.title: Technique: pick your gap before the bird comes
steps: Choose an opening in the canopy to the north and watch only that gap.
When a bird enters it, mount the gun early and swing through.
Never fire at a low bird, or at one toward the house or field.

skill.title: Skill of the week: tagging and reporting a deer
skill.principle: **Core principle:** the work after the shot matters. A tag and a report are part of the hunt. Learn them before you need them.

sections.title: Before the hunt (tonight, 5 minutes)
steps: 1. Open the NCWRC Regulations Digest and find the deer harvest reporting section.
2. Note how the report is made and how soon it must be made. Write it on a card.
3. Put the card, a pen and the cord in your pocket.

sections.title: After a deer is down
steps: 1. Unload. Safety on. Wait a few minutes, then approach from behind.
2. Fill out the tag right away, as the Digest says.
3. Gut and cool the meat within the hour.
4. Make the report as the card says. Log the date and the details.

details.title: Tap to open: why do it tonight
paragraphs: Rules for tagging and reporting change by season and by method. Reading the current Digest before the hunt means no guessing with a deer on the ground.

skill.checkpoint: **Checkpoint:** send a "note:" message with the reporting steps you wrote on your card, in your own words.

land.intro: Today you learn where the loop trail meets the swamp. Make notes on the walk out.
steps: Count your steps from the yard to the Loop North Elbow, and from the sit to the Junction.
Run the thread test at 5:25 and 8:00. Write down which way it points each time.
Walk the swamp edge and look for fresh tracks in the mud. Note the size and the direction.
Look for a deer trail within 100 yards of your sit. Note which way it runs.
Send a "note:" message with what you found. Next week's plan will use it.

safety: **Shooting arc:** north, northwest and northeast. Never beyond east or west. NEVER south. The house is SW, the field is SE, the neighbor is south.
Buckshot and slugs need the ground behind them.
Hunter orange on, hat and vest. Real hunting ends about 9:00. Be unloaded and out.
Mild and damp at dawn, about 55°F. Wet leaves and roots are slick. Walk slowly with the red light, and watch for holes and stumps near the swamp edge.
Warm weather: if you take a deer, cool the meat within the hour. Do not leave it in the sun.
Bear and fox are in the area. Slugs are for defense only.
hunts.regs: Check the NCWRC Regulations Digest for season dates, deer tagging and reporting, bag limits and migratory bird requirements.
hunts.gaps: No hunting entries in your Daily Notes this week. The National Weather Service page was out of date, so the hourly table came from another forecast service with no gust figures and no Friday-night details. The moonrise time was not dated on its source page and may be for Friday night. Legal light is calculated from sunrise. The Digest was not checked directly for the crow day rule or the reporting steps.
